audit.whatIsWrong: Four chart rows are the exact opposite of what the page's own whys say, and of the packet.
audit.why: whys[1] ends 'this level belongs to him' under a row credited to Swain; whys[2] says 'respect his pattern and deny solo kills' under another Swain row; whys[3] says 'you can finally punish every Quickdraw step-up' under Skill, and whys[4] describes your level 6 as a conversion window under Skill. The packet reads Skill, Graves, Graves, Swain, Swain, Swain, Swain, and the mirror already set its chart to the packet.
audit.corrected: win[1]/phases[1].side and win[2]/phases[2].side to Graves; win[3]/phases[3].side and win[4]/phases[4].side to Swain.

audit.why: Spike order is right: his Quickdraw window at 2-3, your 4-5 punish window, your level 6, your first item. Only the reason inside spikes[3] was wrong.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three errors: Graves's resistances are called 'passive armor' in four places, Smoke Screen is still treated as a blind ('your W blind spot'), and whys[3] tells you to Q 'into the stunned window'.
audit.why: New Destiny is the shotgun and reload mechanic — four bullets that cannot pass through units, with a knockback on non-champions. The armour and MR come from True Grit on Quickdraw, doubled when he dashes toward a champion, and refreshed by his attacks. Smoke Screen reduces sight range and slows on impact; it blinds nobody. And Nevermove roots — it produces no stun, so there is no stunned window to burst into.
audit.corrected: Resistances credited to True Grit on Quickdraw, Smoke Screen described as a sight-range cut, and the fake stun replaced with the real sequence: root on the wave's return pass, then pull.

audit.why: Trading around Quickdraw is the right axis. Worth knowing it is 16s at rank 1 but drops as his attacks lower it, so it is not a cooldown you can simply count down.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing mentions that End of the Line detonates on terrain.
audit.why: It explodes after 1 second or on colliding with terrain, so against a wall he can cut your retreat line — and Swain has no dash to leave through it.
audit.corrected: Written into early and mid: hold Flash for the wall angle, not for the damage.

edits.before: Graves wins the range war at Level 1 — his passive armor and shotgun burst let him auto-trade freely before your E root is available, so match-hit only with Q tip and concede the poke.
edits.after: Graves wins the range war at Level 1 — four bullets an attack that cannot pass through units, all before your E exists, so trade at Q tip only and concede the poke for now.

edits.before: Full kit does not overcome Quickdraw's repositioning: he dashes into your W blind spot, bursts, and dashes out before your E lands the root — respect his pattern and deny solo kills.
edits.after: Full kit does not beat Quickdraw's repositioning: he dashes in, bursts, and leaves before the wave returns to root — and Smoke Screen cuts your sight range, it does not blind you.

edits.before: With wave control near your side, you can finally punish every Quickdraw step-up: W the projected landing zone, E the root as his dash decelerates, and Q into the stunned window.
edits.after: With the wave near your side you finally punish every Quickdraw step-up: slow the landing zone with W, throw E past him so the return pass roots, then pull and Q the stack.

edits.before: Liandry's Torment burns through his passive armor stacks and your root combos are now kill-threatening — force every fight on Quickdraw's cooldown while his build is incomplete.
edits.after: Liandry's burns through the True Grit resistances Quickdraw stacks, and your root combos now kill — force every fight while his dash is spent and his build unfinished.

edits.before: Liandry's Torment burning through his self-made armor stacks is your clearest carry window — force fights the moment it completes, exclusively on Quickdraw's cooldown.
edits.after: Liandry's burning through the True Grit resistances Quickdraw grants him is your clearest carry window — force fights the moment it completes, on his dash cooldown.

edits.before: Proc his passive armor stacks by walking into short trades, then backing before Demonic Ascension can drain him
edits.after: Dash at you with Quickdraw for the doubled True Grit stacks, trade short, and leave before your drain starts

edits.before: Level 1 is Graves's range war — his shotgun burst and passive armor let him walk up and trade without fearing your W delay or your rootless kit. Last-hit at safe distance with Q and do not step into his auto range to probe a fight you cannot follow up. The chip he deals here is real and your sustain is not online yet, so absorb the poke and deny him solo kills by staying out of his extended trade window.
edits.after: Level 1 is Graves's range war — a four-bullet shotgun and a reload he can hide behind let him walk up and trade against a rootless Swain. Last-hit at range with Q and do not step in to probe a fight you cannot follow up. Watch the walls too: End of the Line detonates on terrain, so hugging your own wall hands him a free line — hold Flash for that angle, not for the damage. Absorb the chip and deny him the extended trade.

edits.before: Once you have all three abilities Graves still controls the lane through Quickdraw — his dash lets him angle into your W blind spot and trade out before your E can land the root. Play the wave near your side of the lane so he must close distance, then punish every Quickdraw overstep: W the landing zone, E the root as he decelerates, Q the burst. At Level 6 Demonic Ascension changes the math on his burst combos — bait his full rotation, drain it, and recast Demonflare if he tries to dash out of the chain.
edits.after: With all three abilities Graves still controls the lane through Quickdraw — the dash angles him in and out before the wave can come back and root. Hold the wave near your side so he must close, then punish every overstep: slow the landing spot with W, throw E past him so the return pass catches him, pull, then Q the stacked bolts. Never retreat along a wall while End of the Line is up. At 6 the maths changes — bait his full rotation, drain it, and save Demonflare for his dash out.

edits.before: Burn E on the wave. Fight outside R range when committed. Waste W blind. Don't spend your ultimate on chip — it is the kill window.
edits.after: Burn E on the wave. Fight outside R range when committed. Waste W on empty ground. Don't spend your ultimate on chip — it is the kill window.

notes: Graves has no armour on his passive — New Destiny is the shotgun and reload; the resistances are True Grit on Quickdraw, doubled when he dashes toward a champion and refreshed by his autos. That was stated wrongly in four places and it changes the advice, because the resistances arrive with the dash you are trying to punish. Smoke Screen was still being treated as a blind in whys[2]; it reduces sight range and slows on impact. whys[3] told the player to Q 'into the stunned window' — Nevermove roots and never stuns. Four chart rows flipped in matched pairs; they were contradicting the page's own whys text sentence for sentence.
